blurb: Rare Japanese mastiff from Shikoku, built from native and European breeds
description: The Tosa, or Japanese Mastiff, is a rare, very large dog from Japan's Shikoku island with a short, smooth red, brindle or fawn coat; some countries restrict it.
answer: The Tosa, also called the Japanese Mastiff, is a rare large breed that originated in Tosa on the island of Shikoku, Japan, in the second half of the 19th century. Size varies widely, with Japanese-bred dogs often weighing about 36 to 61 kg and dogs bred elsewhere frequently heavier.

body: The breed was developed in Tosa, Shikoku (present-day Kōchi), starting from the native Shikoku-Inu. From the 1870s these dogs were crossed with European breeds including the Old English Bulldog, English Mastiff, Saint Bernard, German Pointer, Great Dane and Bull Terrier to produce a larger, more powerful dog for dog-fighting competitions, and it became the only breed legally allowed in Japanese dog fighting. Breeding peaked between 1924 and 1933. The Tosa was introduced to South Korea in 1955.
Ownership of the Tosa is banned or restricted in a number of countries, including the United Kingdom under the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991.

Size varies considerably. Japanese-bred dogs generally weigh between 36 and 61 kg, while breeders outside Japan have focused on much larger dogs that can weigh 60 to 90 kg. The coat is short and smooth, usually red, brindle or fawn and occasionally dull black. In Japan the dogs are likened to sumo wrestlers and are sometimes shown in wrestling regalia.

Coat maintenance is described as usually minimal. Sources give little detail on exercise needs; as with any large, powerful dog, consistent handling and regular activity are generally recommended.

faq.q: Is the Tosa banned in some countries?
faq.a: Yes. Ownership is banned or legally restricted in a number of countries, including the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland, Denmark and New Zealand.

faq.q: How big does a Tosa get?
faq.a: Size varies a lot. Japanese-bred Tosas generally weigh about 36 to 61 kg, while dogs bred outside Japan are often considerably heavier.

faq.q: Is the Tosa recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 260 in Group 2, with Japan as the country of origin.
